subject: Pen test vendor credentials, methodology, and remediation cadence
messages:
From: Rebecca Lin <rebecca.lin@acme-corp.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samuel Jones <samuel.jones@acme-corp.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: pen test report validity + vendor credentials

Hi Irene / Monica,

Hope you’re well — Acme’s security team is validating third-party controls for our upcoming data processing assessment. We received your SOC2 report already; thanks for that. Our assessor is asking for two additional items before we can move forward:

1) A recent penetration test executive summary or report (redacted fine) and the date the engagement was completed.
2) The vendor credentials / scope / methodology so we can confirm they follow recognized standards (e.g., OWASP/NIST, blackbox/graybox scope).

Two quick clarifications we need: what is your standard cadence for pen testing (annual? continuous?), and how do you handle remediation validation (re-test, evidence of fixes, or exception logs)?

Can you share a redacted report and a short note on your methodology and vendor selection? We’re on a fairly tight procurement timeline and would appreciate an answer by end of next week.

Thanks — Rebecca
Rebecca Lin
Senior Information Security Manager, Acme Corp
rebecca.lin@acme-corp.com

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rebecca Lin <rebecca.lin@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: pen test report validity + vendor credentials

Rebecca — thanks for the note and the specifics. Short answers up front: annual external penetration test (rolling schedule) + continuous internal vuln scanning; remediation validated by the vendor for critical/important findings and by our internal security team for verification evidence.

I’ll attach a redacted summary of the most recent external engagement and the vendor credential pack. High level on methodology below — I’ll ask Mina to add a few more technical details.

- Scope: public-facing inference endpoints, control plane access paths, admin console auth flows. Customer data stores and private VPC deployments are excluded unless the customer requests (we do isolated assessments on-prem where required).
- Methodology: blended assessment (blackbox web testing + authenticated graybox API checks) aligned to OWASP Top 10, SANS, and NIST SP 800-115 testing techniques.
- Firm vetting: we use accredited third-party firms with OSCP/CREST-qualified testers and a minimum 5 years of application security consulting experience.
- Cadence: annual full external test; quarterly triage of high/critical findings from automated scans.

Attachments: PenTest_Summary_Redacted_2026-04.pdf, ThirdPartySec_Credentials.pdf

I’ll follow up with Mina for remediation verification detail and an ETA for any outstanding tickets.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Security Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rebecca Lin <rebecca.lin@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Apr 2026 14:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: pen test report validity + vendor credentials

Hi Rebecca — adding technical context on methodology and remediation acceptance criteria.

1) Testing standards: ThirdPartySec performed a blended engagement. Attack surface mapping followed NIST 800-115, checks mapped to OWASP Top 10 2021, and API tests included authentication, authorization, rate-limiting, and KV cache poisoning scenarios.

2) Credentials: ThirdPartySec provided tester CVs and corporate liability insurance details (attached in ThirdPartySec_Credentials.pdf). They are CREST-affiliated and have performed cloud-native inference service testing for other SaaS vendors.

3) Remediation and verification: For high/critical findings we require vendor-provided re-test evidence. Our process: vendor submits a re-test report or PoC demonstrating remediation -> internal security reproduces fix in a staging environment -> closure. For medium/low findings we track mitigations and monitor via weekly automated scans; we re-test on the next scheduled external assessment or earlier if requested by the customer.

4) Report validity window: We consider an external pen test report valid for 12 months from completion for procurement purposes. If a customer has a shorter validity requirement, we’ll coordinate an addendum or targeted re-test.

If you have SOC2-specific questions about how these findings are mapped to controls, we can provide the mapping doc.

Regards,
Mina
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Rebecca Lin <rebecca.lin@acme-corp.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samuel Jones <samuel.jones@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 08:49:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: pen test report validity + vendor credentials

Thanks Mina / Irene — that is helpful. A couple of follow-ups:

- Acme requires CREST or equivalent affiliation for tester credentials — your note says ThirdPartySec is CREST-affiliated; can you confirm which testers were on the engagement (names and certs) so we can cross-check?
- For remediation validation: for high/critical items we need a vendor re-test report or signed statement within 90 days of the initial report. Is that your typical SLA?

Also, we need confirmation that the testing scope included the admin console authentication flow (specifically session handling) — the summary shows inference endpoints, but our risk team is particularly sensitive to console auth.

Best,
Rebecca

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rebecca Lin <rebecca.lin@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: pen test report validity + vendor credentials

Rebecca — Karthik from Product Security here. Quick confirmations to close your procurement gate:

- Tester roster: ThirdPartySec engagement lead was "Alan Mercer, CREST-CCT, OSCP"; senior tester on auth flows was "Priya Suresh, OSCP". We’ve attached the signed vendor credential pack (ThirdPartySec_Credentials.pdf) which includes the tester CVs and cert numbers.
- SLA for vendor re-test: our standard contractual requirement is 90 days for remediation + re-test of high/critical findings when the customer requires it. ThirdPartySec provided a re-test window and produced a re-test addendum for the April engagement; we’ve included the re-test confirmation in the PenTest_Summary_Redacted_2026-04.pdf attachment (redacted personal data).
- Admin console: yes — the admin console authentication and session handling were explicitly in-scope. The summary includes a single medium finding related to session cookie attributes; that was remediated and re-tested by ThirdPartySec (see remediation tab in the attached Remediation_Timeline_2026-05.xlsx).

If you need a notarized attestation from the vendor or an extension to the re-test SLA in contract language, Monica can coordinate that with procurement.

Thanks for the diligence — happy to hop on a short call if you want to walk the artifacts together.

— Karthik
Director, Product Security, Redwood Inference

Monica/Irene — Acme procurement confirms this satisfies our security gate for contract execution. We’ll include the re-test confirmation clause in our purchase order. Thanks for the fast turnaround.
